params.body:
## Why a bare confirmation is the wrong shape here

Clicking "Car-Pass aanvragen" on staging asked "Car-Pass aanvragen?" with Annuleren / Bevestig and nothing else. That is the shape of a harmless toggle, and this is not one.

`CarpassController::carpassRequest()` sends `odometerReading` together with `odometerReadingDate = date('Y-m-d')`. The mileage standing on the vehicle sheet is therefore published **today** into an official Belgian register, under the dealer's VAT number, and the registration is invoiced. A wrong mileage on the sheet becomes a wrong public reading that can only be repaired through Car-Pass's own portal. A confirmation that hides the very number it is about to register invites a blind click.

## What the old screen did

The confirmation is not something to invent: it already existed and still sits in the working tree as `resources/js/carpass.js`, bound to the `carpass_init_switch` checkbox of the classic own-stock list. That list is gone, so the file had quietly stopped running: nothing calls `carpass.init` any more, its success branch still called `$.toast(...)` (jquery.toast was removed a while back), and its `data.status == 'ongoing'` branch is unreachable because `handleVhrResult()` turns any non-`PROCESSED` status into an error. Three working dialogs had simply fallen out of the product.

What that file did, and what this PR restores in Livewire:

1. **Before sending** — a dialog listing chassis number, mileage and first registration date, each value in bold. So yes: the old screen showed exactly the three facts Shane asked for.
2. **On an ordinary issue** — a dialog whose title is Car-Pass's own message, with mileage and chassis as two **editable** fields, prefilled. Confirmed sends a `correction` on the same request.
3. **On an unknown chassis number (issue 131)** — the same two editable fields and three buttons (`VIN klopt`, `VIN corrigeren`, cancel), plus one rule nobody would invent: **if the user edited either field, pressing the confirm button still sends a `correction`**; only untouched values send a `confirm`. Pressing deny always sends a correction.

So the answer to "did the old flow allow editing" is yes — but only after Car-Pass pushed back, never at the first confirmation. This PR keeps that split: the first dialog shows the numbers and offers no editor (cancel and fix the sheet), the two later dialogs edit.

## What the dialog now shows

Before sending, built from `Vehicle::carpass_confirmation` so it cannot drift from what is sent:

- the vehicle as the row names it: make, model, build year, and the internal number underneath;
- the mileage with thousands separated (`120 000 km`), and the date it is registered under (today);
- the chassis number that will be sent, and the first registration date;
- one sentence saying the registration is invoiced and that a wrong mileage should be corrected on the sheet first.

The numbers shown are the numbers sent: a request from the list carries no `chassis` and no `mileage` of its own, so `carpassRequest()` falls back to the vehicle, which is what the dialog printed. Pinned by a test.

`carpassRequest()` gained explicit `$chassis` and `$mileage` parameters alongside the `$action` parameter from PR 310, for the same reason: a Livewire update request carries only `_token` and `components`, so `request()->get('mileage')` is always empty there and a correction typed in the dialog had no honest way in. The classic route still reads the request; the other three callers (daily task, partner API, `forceUpdateCarpass`) pass nothing and are unchanged.

## No second click while a request is in flight

`carpassRequest()` does `sleep(1)` and then polls Car-Pass up to 21 times. Several seconds pass, and until now the screen showed nothing at all, so a dealer would click again — a second billed registration attempt.

The chip now carries its own Alpine state: it disables itself and reads "Bezig met registreren..." from the moment a call leaves until the `$wire` promise settles, for the initial request and for the confirm/correct follow-ups alike. `wire:loading` was not used because the follow-ups arrive through events and `wire:target` has no reliable handle on those; driving it off the `$wire` promise covers every path with one mechanism.

The browser-side disable is **not** treated as sufficient on its own, because the cost is money: `runCarpass()` takes a 120-second cache lock per vehicle and refuses a second request while one is running. Both are pinned by tests.

## The unknown-chassis dialog no longer claims more than we know

Its text read: "Bevestig het, dan legt Car-Pass de wagen aan." Nothing in the code supports that. What `handleVhrResult()` documents is only that a confirmed unknown VIN yields a public URL **without** a history document; whether Car-Pass thereby registers a vehicle or merely keeps our observation is not knowable from our side. The text now says only that Car-Pass does not know the number, that confirming registers the reading under it, that the resulting Car-Pass carries no history, and that confirming must happen the same day (Car-Pass answers 400 when a confirmation is a day late). Recorded as X-91, with V-19 as a question for Car-Pass rather than for Ilse.

Note for the reviewer: on the beta environment **every** chassis number is unknown, because their test database holds no real vehicles. That is why this dialog looks like the normal path on staging; in production it should be rare (imports, oldtimers, typos). No environment check appears in the user-facing text.

## Dead code removed

`resources/js/carpass.js` and its `window.carpass` global are gone: nothing called them (the public website's Car-Pass modal is plain DOM and does not touch the global), and the Livewire path now carries all three dialogs. `BuildContractTest` and the repo CLAUDE.md dropped `window.carpass` from the globals contract with that reason written down.

## Documentation

- R S3-2.2 moves from *betwist* to *code* and describes what the confirmation shows; **X-24** (which was exactly this finding, open since the code read-through) is closed.
- New: R S3-2.18 (shown equals sent), R S3-2.19 (no second click, browser and server), R S3-2.20 (issue opens the correction dialog; a refusal without an issue stays a message), R S3-2.21 (edited field makes a confirm a correction; empty input never leaves).
- R S3-2.17 rewritten for the three buttons, the honest wording and the same-day rule.
- New finding X-91; new question V-19; O-04 marked half done (the word "aanvragen" on the button itself still overstates nothing and understates everything).
- `92-testdekking.md` and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` regenerated.

## Verification

`php artisan test` — full suite green except `BuildStampTest`, which reads `.git/HEAD` and fails only because this branch was built in a git worktree (`.git` is a file there). The required filter `OwnStockList|Carpass|CarPass|RulesCoverage|StylesheetSyntax|BuildContract|SmokeTest` is 191/191 green. No outbound call is made anywhere: the controller is replaced by a stand-in, so the Outbound seal is never even consulted.
params.title: A Car-Pass request now shows what it will register
